rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī allows that mentioning only good may be an instance of ellipsis, with the implied contrast understood.
rows.anchor: فلا يبعد أن تكون الآية من باب الاكتفاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says only good is mentioned because the verse followed glad tidings to the Prophet of conquests and successive blessings.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما اقتصر عليه لما أن سبب نزول الآية ما آتى الله تعالى نبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من البشارة بالفتوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Things divide into five good-and-evil combinations, but only wholly good and predominantly good things exist in the world; evil is not intended in itself and serves a greater good decreed through wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقيل لما أن الأشياء باعتبار الشر وعدمه تنقسم إلى خمسة أقسام الأول ما لا شر فيه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Painful bloodletting, cupping, bitter medicine, and surgery are rightly accepted because they bring health; similarly, apparent evils in divine decree are means to greater good.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن الفصد ة الحجامة وشرب الدواء الكريه وقطع السلعة ونحوها من الامور المؤلمة لكونه وسيلة حصول الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report warns people not to accuse God in what befalls them personally; no authority or grading is supplied.
rows.anchor: لا تتهم الله تعالى على نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says not to hate trials because they harvest the hypocrites; no authority or grading is supplied.
rows.anchor: لا تكرهوا الفتن فإن فيها حصاد المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says that without sin, a greater danger would be feared: self-admiration.
rows.anchor: لو لم تذنبوا لخفت عليكم ما هو أكبر من ذلك العجب العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The small evil entailed by great benefits is forgiven as a means to them; what leads to good counts as good, so incidental evil falls within “in Your hand is good.”
rows.anchor: فما قدر من المفاسد لتضمنه المصالح العظيمة اغتفر ذلك القدر اليسير فى جنبها لكونه وسيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine decree follows the shared scriptural principle of securing benefits and warding off harms; omitting a small evil would forfeit greater good and itself cause greater evil.
rows.anchor: أحكام القضاء والقدر كما قالوا : جارية على سنن ما اتفقت عليه الشرائع كلها من النظر إلى جلب المصالح وذب المفاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the maxim that nothing in existence could be more excellent than what is; Islamic sages adopted it, and the author dismisses its critics.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب ليس فى الإمكان أبدع مما كان وقد درج حكماء الإسلام عليه ولا يعبأ بمن وجه سهام الطعن إليه

rows.speaker: شرح الهياكل
rows.claim: Evil is decreed incidentally because some great goods entail small evil; leaving those goods to avoid it would produce greater evil, so the resulting evil is good by this consideration.
rows.anchor: أن الشر مقضى بالعرض وصادر بالتبع لما أن بعض ما يتضمن الخيرات الكثيرة قد يستلزم الشر القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This account neither makes the best outcome obligatory for God nor conflicts with “He is not questioned about what He does”: divine wisdom, generosity, and beneficence keep Him from blameworthy acts.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا من القول بوجوب الاصلح ولا ينافيه ( لا يسئل عما يفعل ) إذ لا يفعل ما يسئل عنه كرما وحكمة وجودا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
rows.anchor: نزلت في وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
rows.anchor: نزلت في وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the address was revealed about the Christian delegation from Najrān.
rows.anchor: وفد نصارى نجران قاله السدى والحسن وابن زيد

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr is also cited for the view that the address concerns the Christian delegation from Najrān.
rows.anchor: الحسن وابن زيد ومحمد بن جعفر بن الزبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn Jurayj report that it was revealed about the Jews of Medina.
rows.anchor: وروى عن قتادة والربيع وابن جريج أنها نزلت في يهود المدينة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī says it concerns both groups of the People of the Book; a later verifier prefers this because the wording is general.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو علي الجبائي أنها نزلت في الفريقين من أهل الكتاب واستظهره بعض المحققين لعمومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿālaw means “come” or “come here.”
rows.anchor: تعالوا ( أي هلموا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes kalimah to mean speech; its use for a full utterance is a metonymic figure, though extending it to an incomplete compound has no attested precedent.
rows.anchor: أي كلام كما قال الزجاج واطلاقها على ذلك في كلامهم من باب المجاز المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis treats kalimah as metaphor; al-Ālūsī considers that interpretation plausible.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه من باب الاستعارة وليس بالبعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lightened reading has kasra on kāf and a quiescent lām, with transfer of the vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( كلمة ) بكسر الكاف وإسكان اللام على التخفيف والنقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, and Qatāda explain sawāʾ as justice.
rows.anchor: أي عدل قاله ابن عباس والربيع وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ may mean equal: Torah, Gospel, and Qurʾān do not differ on this principle, or all revealed laws agree on it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ( سواء ) مصدر بمعنى مستوية أي لا يختلف فيها التوراة والانجيل والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading makes sawāʾ genitive as an adjective of kalimah; another reading puts it in the accusative as a cognate adverb.
rows.anchor: وهو في قراءظة الجمهور مجرور على أنه نعت لكلمة وقري بنصبه على المصدر +

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “between us and you” depends on sawāʾ.
rows.anchor: ( بيننا وبينكم ) متعلق بسواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That we worship only God” means that both parties affirm His oneness in worship and devote worship exclusively to Him.
rows.anchor: بأن نوحده بالعبادة ونخلص فيها وفي موضع ( أن )

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ gives two parses for an lā naʿbuda: genitive as an appositive to kalimah, or nominative as predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو الابقاء الأول الجر على البدلية من ( كلمة ) والثاني الرفع على الخبرية لمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an did not govern the clause, it could be explanatory; another parse completes the sentence at sawāʾ and makes the following prepositional phrase the predicate before an lā naʿbuda as subject.
rows.anchor: ولو لا عمل ( أن ) لجاز أن تكون تفسيرية وقيل : إن الكلام تم على ( سواء ) ثم استؤنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not associating anything means neither assigning another being a share in the right to worship nor considering it worthy of worship; this is more likely foundational than mere repetition, though some call it emphasis.
rows.anchor: لا نجعل غيره شريكا له في استحقاق العبادة ولا نراه أهلا لأن يعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation “we associate no thing from among forms of idolatry” is very remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد ( لانشرك به شيئا ) من الشرك وهو بعيد جدا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains taking one another as lords as obeying one another in disobedience to God; the ḥadīth of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim supports this.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن جريج ويؤيده ما أخرجه الترمذي وحسنه من حديث عدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: In a ḥasan report, ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim says they did not worship their religious authorities; the Prophet explained that they followed them when they made lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله فقال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : أما كانوا يحللون لكم ويحرمون

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrimah says taking one another as lords refers to some people prostrating to others.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة أن هذا الاتخاذ هو سجود بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation points to Jewish belief that Ezra is God's son and Christian belief that Christ is God's son.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو مثل اعتقاد اليهود في عزير أنه ابن الله واعتقاد النصارى في المسيح نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “our” refers to people, not to all possible beings such as idols, since the People of the Book did not worship idols.
rows.anchor: وضمير نا على كل تقدير للناس لا للممكن وإن أمكن حتى يشمل الأصنام لأن أهل الكتاب لم يعبدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “some of us” hints that the authorities are members of the same human kind as their followers, so cannot be their lords.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بالبعض نكتة وهي الإشارة إلى أنهم بعض من جنسنا فكيف يكونون اربابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the addressees made others gods alongside God rather than instead of Him; the response takes “besides God” to mean apart from God alone, or says shirk cannot rationally coexist with acknowledging His lordship.
rows.anchor: إن المخاطبين لم يتخذوا البعض أربابا من دون الله بل اتخدوهم آلهة معه سبحانه ( أجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Christians have the greatest share in the prohibitions listed here.
rows.anchor: وللنصارى سود الله تعالى حظهنم الحظ الأوفر من هذه المنهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says that turning away means refusing agreement with the shared message of the revealed books and messengers after it is presented; the proof is then established against them.
rows.anchor: المراد فان تولوا عن موافقتكم فيما ذكر مما اتفق عليه الكتب والرسل بعد عرضه عليهم فاعلموا أنهم لزمتهم الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading they refuse out of obstinacy, and “be witnesses” challenges them to acknowledge the truth or indirectly exposes their refusal.
rows.anchor: وإنما أبو اعنادا فقولوا لهم : أنصفوا واعترفوا بأنا على الدين الحق وهو تعجيز لهم أو هو تعريض بهم

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some verifiers prefer the interpretation that calling them to witness their Islam indirectly makes them admit they are not Muslims.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب بعض المحققين وقيل : المراد فان تولوا فقولوا : إنا لا نتحاشى عن الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view reads the reply as declaring that Muslims do not shrink from Islam or fear anyone and do not conceal their faith as the addressees conceal their unbelief.
rows.anchor: فإنا لا نخفي إسلامنا كمت أنكم تخافون وتخفون كفركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this interpretation fits hypocrites among the People of the Book, who hide from fear, but not these openly professing opponents.
rows.anchor: إنما يحسن لو كان الكلام في منافقي أهل الكتاب لان المنافقين هم الدين يخافون فيخفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallaw is a past-tense verb here; reading it as tatwallaw would misalign the address and leave no valid response, since faqulū addresses the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: ( وتولوا ) هنا ماض ولا يجوز أن يكون التقدير تتولوا لفساد المعنى لان ( فقولوا ) خطاب للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse absolves God's prophets after the People of the Book's accusation against God; another view calls it a refutation of Jesus's worshippers.
rows.anchor: تنزيه لأنبياء الله تعالى عليهم الصلاة والسلام إثر تنزيه الله تعالى عن نسبة ما افتراه أهل الكتاب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the verse as a denial and refutation directed at those who worship Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تكذيب ورد على عبدة عيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports through Ibn Isḥāq and others that Abū Rāfiʿ al-Quraẓī asked whether Muḥammad wanted them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; a Najrān Christian leader asked the same, and the Prophet denied this and said he was not sent or commanded to call people to worship anyone but God; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن إسحق وغيره عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال قال أبو رافع القرظي حين اجتمعت الاحبار من اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a man asked whether they could greet the Prophet as they greeted one another and prostrate to him; the Prophet said to honor the prophet and give people their due, for none should be prostrated to besides God, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الحسن قال : بلغني أن رجلا قال : يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض افلا نسجد لك

rows.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abī Ḥātim says some Jews made people serve them by distorting scripture from its proper place, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم قال : كان ناس من يهود يتعبدون الناس من دون ربهم بتحريفهم كتاب الله تعالى عن موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase mā kāna can mean that such conduct is not valid, not appropriate, or not permitted.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما يصح وقيل : ما ينبغي وقيل : لا يجوز لأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the person bashar hints at the reason for the ruling: human nature is incompatible with the claim the unbelievers attribute to those noble prophets.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالبشر إيذائا بعلة الحكم فان البشرية منافية للأمر الذي اسنده الكفرة إلى أولئك الكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposed lām phrase is the predicate of kāna and the clause with an is its subject; an implied conjunction is needed for sound meaning, since many humans received scripture and prophethood.
rows.anchor: والجاز خبر مقدم لكان والمنسبك من ( أن ) والفعل بعد اسمها ولا بد لاستقامة المعنى من ملاحظة العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma emphasizes the enormity of a prophet making this claim after the divine gift: if it is impossible after a delay, it is even more impossible immediately.
rows.anchor: وعطف الفعل على منصوب ان بثم تعظيما لهذا القول فانه إذا انتقى بعد مهلة كان انتقاؤه بدونها اولى واحرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ḥukm means wisdom, as explained earlier.
rows.anchor: والحكم بمعنى الحكمة وقد تقدم معناه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says ʿibād is the plural of ʿabd in the sense of worship; ʿabīd instead denotes servitude that can belong to someone other than God.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وهو هنا من العبادة ولم يقل عبيدا لأنه من العبودية وهي لا تمتنع أن تكون لغير الله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains min dūn Allāh as describing people who go beyond God by either associating others or singling them out; the phrase can be an additional adjective or circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: كما قال الجبائي فان التجاوز متحقق فيهما حتما ثم إن هذا الايتاء في الآية حقيقة على الروايتين الأوليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's bestowal is literal according to the first two transmitted occasions, but metaphorical in the account about Jewish scholars distorting scripture.
rows.anchor: ثم إن هذا الايتاء في الآية حقيقة على الروايتين الأوليين مجاز على الرواية الأخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-lākin kūnū rabbāniyyīn affirms what was denied: a prophet does not tell people to worship him but tells them to become learned, devout servants of God; the verb is coordinated in the subjunctive.
rows.anchor: إثبات لما نفي سابقا وهو القول المنصوب بأن كأنه قيل : ما كان لذلك البشر أن يقول ذلك لكن يقول كونوا ربانيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some allow the verb indicative based on the meaning “he does not say”; another analysis omits an implied saying and means they should not say that but should be rabbāniyyūn.
rows.anchor: وجوز رفعه على المعنى لأنه في معنى لا يقول وقيل ك يصح عدم تقدير القول على معنى لا تكونوا قائلين لذلك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās define rabbānī as a learned jurist.
rows.anchor: وفسر علي كرم الله وجهه وابن عباس الرباني بالفقيه العالم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī define rabbānī as a wise scholar.
rows.anchor: وقتادة والسدي بالعالم الحكيم

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines rabbānī as wise and God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وابن جبير بالحكيم التقي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines rabbānī as one who manages the affairs of people; the author says these definitions are close.
rows.anchor: وابن زيد بالمدبر امر الناس وهي أقوال متقاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rabbānī is Arabic, not Syriac, according to the sounder view; Abū ʿUbaydah claims Arabs do not know it.
rows.anchor: وهو لفظ عربي لا سرياني على الصحيح + وزعم أبو عبيدة أن العرب لا تعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common derivation relates the word to rabb with emphatic nisba endings; another derives it from rabbān, “educator,” on the pattern of ʿaṭshān.
rows.anchor: وهو منسوب إلى الرب كالهي والألف والنون يزدادان في النسب للبالغة كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bi-phrases explain why people should become rabbānī: they persist in teaching scripture and studying it; knowledge must be joined to practice, since neither alone counts.
rows.anchor: الباء السببية متعلقة بكونوا أي كونوا كذلك بسبب مثابرتكم على تعليمكم الكتاب ودراستكم له والمطلوب أن لا ينفك العلم عن العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other syntactic analyses attach the cause phrase to rabbāniyyīn or treat it as an omitted modifier.
rows.anchor: متعلقة م بربانيين لان فيه معنى الفعل وقيل : بمحذوف وقع صفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirāsah means repetition and can also mean reading; repeating “because you were” marks teaching and reading as distinct, sustained causes of attaining rabbāni status.
rows.anchor: والدراسة التكرار يقال : درس الكتاب أي كرره وتطلق على القراءة وتكرير ( بما كنتم ) للإشعار باستقلال كل من استمرار التعليم واستمرار القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb after kāna suggests continuing teaching and reading that cultivates rabbāni character; teaching is placed first for its greater honor or because the first audience were leaders and the second their subordinates.
rows.anchor: المشعربة جعل خبر ( كان ) مضارعا بالفضل وتحصيل الربانية وقدم تعليم الكتاب على دراسته لوفور شرفه عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes the taught scripture as the Qurʾān and the studied material as fiqh; al-Ālūsī considers it quite remote, despite hints in some early authorities.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأن متعلق التعليم الكتاب بمعنى القرآن ومتعلق الدراسة الفقه وفيه بعد بعيد

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaʿqūb, Abū ʿAmr, and Mujāhid read taʿlamūn as “being knowledgeable.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير ويعقوب وابو عمرو ومجاهد ( تعلمون ) بمعنى عالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadrusūn is also read with doubled dāl or with hamza prefix; both convey the same sense, and the common form may likewise mean teaching it to people.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( تدرسون ) بالتشديد من التدريس وتدرسون من الإدراس بمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage opens by rebuking those who fled for failing to follow the example of the many God-devoted fighters with messengers, although they had even greater reason to do so as the best community.
rows.anchor: كلام مبتدأ سيق توبيخا للمنهزمين أيضا حيث لم يستنوا بسنن الربانيين المجاهدين مع الرسل عليهم الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: ابن حيان
rows.claim: Ibn Ḥayyān and others say kaʾayyin is a simple word coined as such, with an original nūn.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنها بسيطة وضعت كذلك إبتداءا والنون أصلية وإليه ذهب إبن حيان وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The widely held account derives kaʾayyin by compounding the simile particle kāf with ayyin, though the question of ayyin's origin is disputed.
rows.anchor: وهو المشهور : إنها مركبة منأيالمنونة وكاف التشبيه وأختلف فيأيهذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view derives ayyin from the phrase ayy al-rijāl; Ibn Jinnī instead treats it as a verbal noun of awā yaʾwī, “to join,” altered by sound change like ṭayy and shayy.
rows.anchor: فقيل : هي أي التي في قولهم : أي الرجال وقال إبن جني : إنها مصدر أوى يأوى إذا أنضم وأجتمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once compounded, kaʾayyin acquired the abundant quantity sense of kam; they share five properties, while interrogation is rare and accepted by only a few grammarians.
rows.anchor: وحدث فيها بعد التركيب معنى التكثير المفهوم من كم كما حدث في كذا بعد التركيب معنى آخرفكم وكأينبمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: An anecdote offered as evidence for an interrogative sense has Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ask Ibn Masʿūd how many verses are in al-Aḥzāb; he answers seventy-three.
rows.anchor: وأستدل عليه بقول أبي بن كعب لإبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنهما : كائن تقرأ سورة الأحزاب آية فقال : ثلاثا وسبعين

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Kaʾayyin differs from kam in several ways; against Ibn ʿAṣfūr's claim that its measure must be governed by min, Sībawayh explicitly allows otherwise.
rows.anchor: حتى زعم إبن عصفور لزوم ذلك ويرده نص سيبويه على عدم اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line illustrates kaʾayyin with a genitive measure introduced by min.
rows.anchor: أطرد اليأس بالرجاء ( فكائن ) ألما حم يسره بعد عسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾayyin and kadhā share compounding, indeclinability, ambiguity, and need for a measure; unlike kadhā, kaʾayyin takes no clause-initial position and its measure is usually genitive with min.
rows.anchor: فتوافقها كذافي أربعة أمور : التركيب والبناء والإبهام والإفتقار إلى التمييز

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kūfans allow kadhā plus a singular or plural noun without repetition or conjunction, by analogy to explicit numerals; this affects jurists' numerical readings of such statements.
rows.anchor: الثاني أن تمييزها واجب النصب فلا يجوز جره بمن إتفاقا ولا بالإضافة خلافا للكوفيين أجازوا في غير تكرار ولا عطف

rows.speaker: ابن خروف
rows.claim: Ibn Khurūf claims that grammarians did not use kadhā dirham; Ibn Mālik says it is attested but rare, as reported by Ibn Hishām.
rows.anchor: وزعم إبن خروف أنهم لم يقولوا كذا درهما وذكر إبن مالك أنه مسموع لكنه قليل قاله إبن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing and stopping with tanwīn on kaʾayyin departs from ordinary analogy because its original form was copied; the word has several readings.
rows.anchor: ثم إن إثبات تنوين ( كأين ) على القول المشهور في الوقف والخط على خلاف القياس لما أنه نسخ أصلها

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads kāʾin, with an alif and kasra hamza but no yāʾ; the poem confirms this form, though al-Mubarrad's derivation from kāna is implausible because it explains neither its indeclinability nor its quantity sense.
rows.anchor: والثانية كائنبألف بعدها همزة مكسورة من غير ياء على وزن كأعن كأسم الفاعل وبها قرأ إبن كثير

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads kaʾayyi with yāʾ after the hamza; the explanation treats the two words as fused and the hamza as quiescent.
rows.anchor: والث الثة كأيبياء بعد الهمزة وبها قرأ إبن محيصن ووجهها أنها حذفت الياء الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two additional transmitted forms are kayyin and kaʾin with open kāf; a poetic citation supplies the latter, which is explained by deleting one or both yāʾs after compounding.
rows.anchor: والرابعة كيئنبياء ساكنة بعدها همزة مكسورة والخامسة كئنبكاف مفتوحة وهمزة مكسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed kāf has no syntactic governor because it has lost its simile meaning; kaʾayyin is nominative as subject and min nabiyy is its measure, as with kam.
rows.anchor: والكاف لا متعلق لها لخروجها عن معناها ومن قال به كالحوفي فقد تعسف وموضعهما رفع بالإبتداء

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī explicitly says the prophet intended here may mean a messenger.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد من النبي هنا الرسول وبه صرح الطبرسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The famous interpretation from Ibn ʿAbbās takes rabbiyyūn as large groups.
rows.anchor: أي جموع كثيرة وهو التفسير المشهور عن إبن عباس

rows.speaker: إبن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī transmits the poetic evidence from Ḥassān after Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq asks about the meaning.
rows.anchor: رواه إبن الأنباري حين سأله نافع بن الأزرقبقول حسان

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifies the group as one thousand.
rows.anchor: وخصها الضحاك بألف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report from Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr says al-Ḥasan defined rabbiyyūn as learned jurists.
rows.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور عن الحسن أنهم العلماء الفقهاء

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr also transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that rabbiyyūn are learned jurists.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه إبن جبير عن إبن عباس أيضاوعليه فهو منسوب إلى الرب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd distinguishes rabbiyyūn as followers and rabbāniyyūn as rulers.
rows.anchor: وقال إبن زيد : الربيون هم الأتباع والربانيون الولاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may be nisba to ribba, “group,” though the claimed dialectal ḍamma is unverified; another derivation relates it to rabb like rabbānī, irregularly, with readings supporting both vowel forms.
rows.anchor: وعليه فهو منسوب إلى ربة بكسر الراء وكون الضم فيها لغة غير متحقق

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb read qūtila in the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وإبن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوبقتل بالبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading has four syntactic analyses: the verb can supply the predicate with an implicit subject; “with him were groups” can be the predicate while the verb clause modifies prophet; the predicate may be omitted as “passed away”; or rabbiyyūn may be raised by the verb as predicate.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر المبتدأ أوجه : أحدها أنه الفعل مع الضمير المستتر فيه الراجع إلى ( كأين )

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: On the doubled passive quttِla, Ibn Jinnī denies an implicit singular subject because doubling conveys plurality; a reply says it can still refer to one prophet since the action is collective, while critics find that less apparent.
rows.anchor: وقريءقتل بالتشديد قال إبن جني : وحينئذ فلا ضمير في الفعل لما في التضعيف من الدلالة على التكثير

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits Ibn Jubayr saying that they had never heard of a prophet killed in battle; al-Ḥasan and others likewise say no prophet was killed in war.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه إبن المنذر عن إبن جبير أنه كان يقول : ما سمعنا قط أن نبيا قتل في القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a prophet was killed in battle, one answer reconciles this with God's promise to aid His messengers by taking victory as elevation of their cause rather than victory over every enemy.
rows.anchor: حمل النصرة الموعود بها في قوله تعالى : ( إنا لننصر رسلنا ) عل ى النصرة بإعلاء الكلمة ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwīn on nabiyy signals magnification.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في ( نبي ) للتعظيم

rows.speaker: الأجهوري
rows.claim: Al-Ajhūrī claims the tanwīn on nabiyy conveys abundance.
rows.anchor: وزعم الأجهوري أنه للتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-mā wahanū is coordinated with the fighting verb and denies the weakness expected after fighting; although it seems to continue the same state, persistence after a new cause is a fresh deed, explaining the resultative fa.
rows.anchor: عطف على قاتلوا على أن المراد عدم الوهن المتوقع من القتال والتلبس بالشيء بعد ورود ما يستدعي خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the resultative construction to “I admonished him but he did not take heed” and “I rebuked him but he did not desist.”
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قولهم : وعظته فلم يتعظ وزجرته فلم ينزجر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Abī Mālik gloss wahn here as incapacity.
rows.anchor: وفسره قتادة وإبن أبي مالك هنا بالعجز

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses wahn as cowardice.
rows.anchor: والزجاج بالجبن أي فما عجزوا أو فما جبنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Because of what befell them in God's path” gives the cause for the denied weakness, not a cause for weakness; its qualification implies the negated state, and mā can be relative or descriptive.
rows.anchor: وهذا علة للمنفي لا للنفي نعم يفهم المنفي من تقييد المثبت بهذا الظرف وماموصولة أو موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronouns refer to all the rabbiyyūn, mā covers hardships of war other than death that affect all; if only survivors, it more aptly covers fear and grief after comrades are killed, fitting the rebuke of those who fled.
rows.anchor: فهي عبارة عما عدا القتل من مكاره الحروب التي تعتري الكل وإن جملا للبعض الباقين بعد قتل الآخرينوهو الأنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On passive readings, if the verb is attached to its overt noun, the pronouns must refer to survivors; the usage resembles saying a clan was killed when deaths occurred but did not annihilate it.
rows.anchor: وأما على القراءتين الأخيرتين أعني قتل وقتلعلى صيغة المبني للمفعول مخففة ومشددة فقد قالوا : إن أسند الفعل إلى الظاهر فالضميران للباقين حتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If qutila is instead assigned to an implicit subject, the pronouns refer to survivors when rabbiyyūn accompanied the prophet in being killed, but to all when they accompanied him in fighting; this fits rumors of the Prophet's death prompting flight.
rows.anchor: إن أسند إلى الضمير كما هو الظاهر الأنسب عند البعض بالتوبيخ على الإنخذال بسبب الأرجاف بقتله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains mā ḍaʿufū as not becoming languid in jihad.
rows.anchor: أي ما فتروا عن الجهاد قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they did not become weak in faith or change their conviction when victory did not come.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما عراهم ضعف في الدين بأن تغير إعتقادهم لعدم النصر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says mā istakānū means they did not turn back from their insight or religion.
rows.anchor: أي ما أرتدوا عن بصيرتهم ولا عن دينهم قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation points to their not submitting to their enemy; istakāna can also mean supplicating.
rows.anchor: ما خضعوا لعدوهم وإليه يشير كلام إبن عباس وكثيرا ما يستعمل إستكان بهذا المعنى وكذا بمعنى تضرع

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Grammarians dispute istakāna's derivation: from sakana on iftiʿāl, with an emphatic lengthening vowel, which al-Ālūsī says is valid and not restricted to poetry despite Abū al-Baqāʾ and Abū Ḥayyān; or from kawn on istafʿal, with extra sīn and wāw-derived alif signaling emphatic seeking of subjugation.
rows.anchor: وأختلف فيه هل هو من السكون فوزنه أفتعل لأن الخاضع يسكن لمن خضع له فألفه للأشباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says the humbled person is like nothing, so seeks from himself the state of existence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنه كالعدم فهو يطلب من نفسه الوجود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and al-Suddī are associated with the view that the verb's implicit subject is the prophet, with the pronouns then referring to survivors or all who fought alongside him.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب قتادة والربيع وإبن أبي إسحاق والسديكما قيلفهما للباقين

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī and Abū ʿAlī offer further derivations of istakānū from expressions for being in a bad state or being humbled; this makes its alif derive from yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعزى ذلك إلى الأزهري وأبي علي وحينئذ فألفه منقلبة عن ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers open the hāʾ in wahanū; kasra is a dialectal reading, and sukūn lightens the kasra.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على فتح الهاء من ( وهنوا ) وقريء بكسرها وهي لغة والفتح أشهر و قريء بإسكانها على تخفيف المكسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause contains an unmistakable indirect rebuke.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام تعريض لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient are praised for enduring hardship and adversity in God's path; God then aids them and raises their standing.
rows.anchor: على مقاساة الشدائد ومعاناة المكاره في سبيله فينصرهم ويعظم قدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient may mean the rabbiyyūn specifically; the explicit noun replaces a pronoun to praise their patience and state the cause of God's love.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصابرين إما الربيون والإظهار في موضع الإضمار للتصريح بالثناء عليهم بالصبر الذي هو ملاك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the patient include everyone, with the rabbiyyūn foremost among them.
rows.anchor: وإما ما يعمهم وغيرهم وهم داخلون في ذلك دخولا أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing statement is a summative conclusion to what precedes, on either interpretation of who the patient are.
rows.anchor: والجملة على التقديرين تذييل لما قبلها
